newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks fall, weighed down by golds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks fall, weighed down by golds.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended weaker on Wednesday for the second day in a row, weighed down by a sliding gold sector that tumbled almost two percent.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell 34.20 points to 6498.14 on turnover of 89.2 million shares worth C$948 million ($682 million). Declining stocks outpaced advancers 569 to 379, while 327 issues were steady.
Eleven of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes were down, led by golds, which shed 177.68 points or 1.96 percent to 8903.53, while the Dow Jones Industrial fell 42.07 to 7718.71 points.

"The gold index was down 177 (points), so that accounted for half the decline, and I guess the other half was accounted for in New York,"said Rolie Bradley, institutional salesman at Maison Placements Canada Inc.
Traders said the market was feeling the effects ahead of triple-witching on Friday, when options, futures and options on futures all expire.
"There's a lot of hesitation going into triple-witching on Friday that skews the market so much," one trader said.

Traders said shares of CS Resources Ltd. attracted lots of attention after PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd. said early on Wednesday that it agreed to acquire CS for C$16 ($11.52) a share and the assumption of C$56 million ($40 million) in debt.
PanCanadian's friendly bid topped a rival offer by Gulf Canada Resources Ltd. Gulf Canada said it would not revise its bid.
CS shares rose C$0.85 to C$15.80 in turnover of more than six million shares, topping Toronto actives.
PanCanadian shares fell C$0.25 to C$29.95 in thin trade, while Gulf rose C$0.15 to C$11.85.
